newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends higher in light volumes.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends higher in light volumes.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures settled broadly higher on a general lack of selling in a thinly-traded session, traders said.
Traders said wheat gained after USDA said U.S. net export sales of wheat during the week ended June 19 totaled 584,100 tonnes, above expectations for 300,000 to 400,000 tonnes.
"We hit (buy) stops in the first hour when there was nothing for sale," a MGE trader said. "I think the weekly export report kind of surprised some folks."
But there was also talk of a return to drier weather conditions in key North Dakota growing areas.

"I think a drier weather scenario for the Dakotas caught people's imagination... Some people think we've got a real disaster on our hands when we really don't," the MGE trader said of differing perceptions of the extent of dryness.
Traders said volumes were light ahead of the release Monday of USDA's acreage and grain stocks reports. The MGE estimated volume in spring wheat futures Thursday at 17.726 million bushels.
"There was not a lot of volume today. Only a couple of the big locals were trading it... probably in anticipation of the USDA report," another floor source said.
MGE spring wheat settled five to 9-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with July up 9-1/2 cents at $3.82-3/4 a bushel. New crop September gained nine cents to close at $3.72-1/2.
